sources.outlet: U.S. District Court, Southern District of Florida (indictment, U.S. v. Ibrahim Khaldoon Hilmi, 26-CR-20238, posted by USAO-SDFL)
sources.quote: Sunshine Senior submitted at least $3.34 billion in false and fraudulent claims to Medicare, the FEHBP, Medicaid, and Commercial Insurers for DME and wound dressings that were medically unnecessary and not provided.
sources.searcher_note: Indictment (PDF) defines Sunshine Senior Solutions LLC as a shell DME supplier billing wound dressings; window Nov 2024 to Sep 2025; says $1.78B processed as paid but nearly all held in suspension by Medicare Part B, about $3.5M deposited. Does not say alginate.

sources.outlet: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Health Care Fraud Unit
sources.quote: In total, ABRH and Sunshine Senior Solutions submitted at least $3.76 billion in fraudulent claims to Medicare, Medicaid, and other insurers, but only approximately $5.7 million was deposited into ABRH and Sunshine Senior Solutions bank accounts.
sources.searcher_note: 2026 takedown case summary: Sunshine Senior Solutions and ABRH billed 'medical equipment and wound dressings' never provided. Its deposited-money figure is far below the lead's $593.6M paid; relevant to the paid-vs-claimed question.

sources.quote: Barlow was charged for 'wound covers' and hundreds of catheters between September 2024 and February of this year, according to Medicare documents he received.
sources.searcher_note: Houston seniors billed by Sunshine Senior Solutions for wound covers and catheters starting Sept 2024; Medicare paid Sunshine about $25,700 for one man; Sunshine no longer enrolled in Medicare as of June 2025.

sources.quote: The payments were all for wound dressings, glucose monitors for diabetes and catheters that they say they never received or needed.
sources.searcher_note: Earliest Almaz coverage found: three women say Medicare paid Almaz Med Supply (Queens) thousands for wound dressings and other supplies they never got. Almaz is named in the surrounding sentences, not in the quote.

sources.quote: Months later, the same company charged Medicare over $8,200 worth of "wound dressings" for her.
sources.searcher_note: Utah woman billed by Almaz Med Supply (named in the preceding lines) for wound dressings; Medicare paid $6,300. Original URL at ksltv.com redirects here.

sources.outlet: Better Business Bureau Serving Metropolitan New York
sources.quote: As of this date, there are 103 Scam Tracker reports on Almaz Med Supply Inc., as well as 11 complaints with BBB.
sources.searcher_note: BBB warning: consumers say Almaz charged Medicare for supplies never ordered; no dressing type or dollar totals on this page.

notes: Both suppliers are named in press and court records for billing Medicare for wound dressings nobody ordered. No source found names alginate specifically, and none gives the $593.6M / $649.2M / 91.4% share or the 494-vs-55 dressings-per-claim numbers. A search snippet said a BBB complaint listed Almaz claims for '120 Alginate or other fiber gelling dressing' at $2,760, but the BBB complaints page fetched without complaint text, so that isn't recorded. Possible tension: DOJ says Sunshine's $1.78B processed-as-paid was nearly all held in suspension by Medicare Part B, with about $3.5M deposited, and dates Sunshine's billing from Nov 2024 (ABC13 says Sept 2024). So whether the lead's 2024 'took $593.6M' means money actually paid out is a question for the judge. KXAN article (Feb 2026, Machutadze) returned 403 and wasn't used. Nothing found dated after 2026-06-30.
